content: Temocillin is a β-lactamase-resistant penicillin that was originally introduced by Beecham and is currently marketed by Eumedica Pharmaceuticals under the brand name Negaban. It is primarily utilized for the treatment of infections caused by multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria. Structurally, it belongs to the carboxypenicillin class of antibiotics. Pharmacologically, temocillin is resistant to β-lactamase enzymes, which makes it effective against certain bacteria that produce these enzymes. However, it is not active against Gram-positive bacteria or bacteria that have altered penicillin-binding proteins. Temocillin demonstrates activity against a range of Gram-negative organisms, including Moraxella catarrhalis, Brucella abortus, Burkholderia cepacia, Citrobacter species, Escherichia coli, Haemophilus influenzae, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pasteurella multocida, Proteus mirabilis, Salmonella typhimurium, and Yersinia enterocolitica. It also shows activity against some strains of Enterobacter species, Morganella morganii, and Serratia species. However, it is not effective against Acinetobacter species or Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Its primary clinical application is in treating infections caused by Enterobacteriaceae, particularly strains that produce extended-spectrum β-lactamases (ESBLs) or AmpC β-lactamases. The standard dosage of temocillin is 2 grams administered intravenously every 12 hours. In severe infections, continuous intravenous infusion may be considered. This involves an initial loading dose of 2 grams intravenously, followed by a 4-gram infusion over 24 hours. For intramuscular administration, 7 mL of sterile water is used for preparation, while continuous infusion is diluted in 48 mL of sterile water to facilitate administration (1 mL per half-hour). To minimize pain during intramuscular injection, sterile 1% lignocaine can be used instead of sterile water. Temocillin can be safely administered to patients with impaired renal function. No dose adjustment is required in cases of mild to moderate renal impairment (creatinine clearance >30 mL/min). However, since temocillin is cleared by hemodialysis, the dose should be administered after dialysis sessions in patients undergoing this treatment. Currently, there is no licensed oral formulation of temocillin. Adverse effects associated with temocillin are similar to those observed with other β-lactam antibiotics. Notably, it has been linked to angioedema and anaphylaxis in patients with penicillin allergies. Animal studies have not demonstrated any association between temocillin use and the induction of Clostridium difficile infections. As with other penicillins, high doses of temocillin may lead to convulsions.
